_comment: v1.12.2 - subsection markers for the Latin of the thirteen Book III excerpts. Both translations were written with their markers already at these boundaries and mark_sections.js skips a field that carries them. Boundaries from Perseus (CTS phi0448.phi002); all thirteen are whole chapters. Two overrides where the Latin Library and Perseus diverge at a section's opening words: III.19.6 (`Qua ex frequentia, Titus Labienus prodit, sed missa oratione` against Perseus' `qua ex frequentia T. Labienus prodit, summissa oratione`) and III.89.4 (`Simul his` against `simul iis`). III.96 is the awkward one and takes an INLINE anchor list instead of the cache: Perseus returns sections numbered 1, 3 and 4 with no 2, having merged the standard 96.1 and 96.2 into a single div. The editions divide at `At hi miserrimo`, so the four anchors are written out here and the numbering comes out right.

overrides.6: Qua ex frequentia, Titus Labienus prodit
